{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status" },
  "read": "Freezing in a big moment isn't a character flaw — the brain under pressure can literally shut down motor patterns that work fine in practice. But right now they're reading the freeze as proof they can't do it, and they're worried the whole team saw it and drew the same conclusion. Both of those stories need to be interrupted fast.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Tell them it's fine, it happens to everyone, no big deal — which feels kind but quietly confirms there's something to be ashamed of and lets them stay stuck in the story that they failed" },
  "mentorMove": "Acknowledge the moment was hard, then immediately reframe what happened in the brain as a normal physiological response that capable athletes learn to work with — not a verdict on who they are. Hold the expectation that they'll compete in the next one.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "They are going back into competition — sitting them out to protect feelings lowers the bar and reinforces avoidance.",
    "The standard for effort and presence stays the same; the freeze doesn't buy them a pass on the next rep or the next game."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Let them tell you what the moment felt like before you explain anything — they need to be heard first.",
    "You can adjust how you put them back in: a smaller moment, a clear role, a cue word they choose — whatever builds the bridge back to trust in themselves."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, come here a second. I saw your face out there and I just want to sit with you for a minute before we do anything else. That moment was hard." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Tell me what was going through your head when it happened — what did it feel like right before you froze?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's what I want you to know: what you felt is your nervous system doing what nervous systems do under high stakes — it flooded, it locked up. That's not weakness, that's a brain that cares. Every competitor I've ever respected has stood exactly where you're standing. The ones who got good at this learned to recognize that feeling and use it. We can work on that together, starting today." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm not pulling you back from these moments — I'm putting you right back in them, because I have high standards for what you're capable of and I've seen enough to know you can get there. Next opportunity comes up, we go. You good with that?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "In the next few practices, build in high-pressure reps by design — short, loud, stakes attached — and debrief them quickly so they accumulate evidence that they can perform when it counts. The goal is to replace the one bad memory with ten reps where they came through, so the freeze stops being their identity and starts being the moment before they figured it out."
}
situation: One of my players froze in the big moment and is now down on themselves.
